lan.topology: workstation in the GARAGE, NUC ~100 ft away in the LIVING ROOM, no Ethernet run between them and none planned: at least one hop is the mesh's wireless backhaul. Design for a measured 1080p60 ~15 Mbps stream, not an assumed wired gigabit path

workstation.gamepad_dongle: CONFIRMED on the workstation 2026-11-03 23:55 (dongle plugged in, pad on): it enumerates as USB VID_045E PID_028E 'Xbox 360 Controller for Windows' (XnaComposite + HID-compliant game controller, IG_00) - i.e. the generic 2.4 GHz receiver EMULATES a wired Xbox 360 controller (XInput). On Linux the in-kernel xpad driver claims 045e:028e with no extra driver, SDL2 has a built-in mapping, no button-mapping screen is needed for THIS pad (keep the first-run mapper for unknown pads). xone/xpadneo stay optional extras. While the pad is OFF the dongle alone may show as a vendor HID device. Sunshine presents whatever the NUC sends via ViGEm (present on the host). The pad is NOT needed on the workstation.

nuc.model: Intel NUC7i5BNK (Baby Canyon, 2017; Michael 2026-11-03). CPU Core i5-7260U Kaby Lake 2C/4T 2.2-3.4 GHz; iGPU Iris Plus Graphics 640 (Gen9.5, 64 MB eDRAM): hardware DECODE H.264, HEVC Main/Main10 8+10-bit up to 4K60, VP9 - NO AV1, no HDMI 2.1, no 4K120. Video out HDMI 2.0a (4K60; via an LSPCON MCDP2800 that the i915 driver handles on kernel 6.8) + Thunderbolt 3 USB-C (DP 1.2). 'K' = slim kit: ONE M.2 2280 SSD slot (SATA or NVMe), NO 2.5-inch bay; 2x DDR4-2133 SO-DIMM (installed RAM/SSD sizes UNKNOWN - couch-doctor reports them). NIC Intel I219-V gigabit (e1000e). Intel Wireless-AC 8265 + Bluetooth 4.2 (so the xpadneo/BT path is physically possible). 4x USB 3.0 Type-A (2 front, one charging; 2 rear), front IR receiver. HDMI CEC: UNVERIFIED (treat as absent). VAAPI = intel-media-driver (iHD) on Ubuntu 24.04; the free intel-media-va-driver package covers Gen9.5 decode.
nuc.tv_input: one dedicated HDMI input on the living-room TV (same TV as the Roku 'MKUltra', LAN 192.168.86.33)
nuc.implications: Default 1080p60 HEVC ~15 Mbps is trivial for this box; 4K60 HEVC decode is in reach if the link allows; AV1 and HDR are OFF in v1 (no AV1 decode; HDR-on-Wayland not a target). Do not hard-code: couch-doctor's vainfo still decides.
